r0-context.finding: Loaded global-crew.md, global-everyone.md, CREW_CONTEXT.md, GLOSSARY.md, the g1-reviewer-handoff.md, the g1-implementer-result.md, and read the actual diff (scripts/race_week_stages.py, tests/unit/scripts/test_race_week_stages.py) plus cited source seams (run.py, artifacts.py, beam_search.py, constants.py, _metadata_session.py, collector.py) and docs/design/race_week_seam.md.

r1-handoff.title: Handoff compliance
r1-handoff.imperative: Did the change do what the handoff asked, within its allowed scope? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r1-handoff.finding: 6/7 close criteria independently confirmed (4 pure stage functions; predict_stage never defaults db_path -- SimpleNamespace threads caller value verbatim, code+test verified; optimize_stage calls generate_report exactly once and never imports write_beam_search_report -- hasattr(rws,'write_beam_search_report')==False, code+test verified; unknown lane raises ValueError before generate_report is invoked, and FantasyBeamSearchResult at beam_search.py:52-63 genuinely has no best_max field, re-verified by reading the dataclass; 31/31 tests pass on independent re-run; simplification_limits --paths passes on independent re-run). BUT the 5th criterion -- 'explain_stage cannot raise under any input, including an exception thrown mid-copy' -- is FALSE as implemented and as claimed in the implementer result. race_week_stages.py:288-289 (explainer_path = Path(explainer_path); stub_path = explainer_path.with_name(...)) execute BEFORE the try block starts at line 291. Live repro: rws.explain_stage('some/stem', None) raises uncaught TypeError (Path(None) rejects NoneType); rws.explain_stage('some/stem', '') raises uncaught ValueError (WindowsPath('.') has an empty name). The implementer's Required-note evidence (b) claims 'The entire function body is wrapped in a broad try/except Exception' -- this is not true, two path-construction lines sit outside the try. No test in test_race_week_stages.py exercises a bad explainer_path, so this gap was not caught by the test suite.

r2-scope.title: Scope drift
r2-scope.imperative: Did the change stay inside allowed scope and respect specific exclusions? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r2-scope.finding: git status --porcelain in the worktree shows exactly the two sanctioned new files (scripts/race_week_stages.py, tests/unit/scripts/test_race_week_stages.py) as untracked additions -- confirmed by my own git status run, not the pasted result. No scripts/race_week.py exists (ls confirms 'No such file or directory'). git status --porcelain | grep '^.. src/' returns none -- zero src/ changes. rws has no write_beam_search_report symbol (hasattr==False) and grep of the new file shows only one generate_report call site. All Specific Exclusions respected. One incidental non-scope item: 'M data/f1_data_2026.db' also appears in git status (Bin, 0 insertions/deletions, same byte size) -- predates any command I ran, not part of the two sanctioned files, and not something either handoff or implementer result mentions; flagged as an out-of-scope observation for Commander (likely a benign WAL/journal touch from an earlier pytest run in this worktree, not a content change) rather than a scope violation of this gate's mandate.

r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding: Test-suite and simplification_limits evidence: solid, reproduced independently (31/31 pass, exact same test names/order as pasted; simplification_limits PASS re-run). Required-note (a) no-double-call and (c) lane-validates-before-generate_report: solid, both code-read-confirmed and test-confirmed. Required-note (b) 'explain_stage never raises': the produced evidence (test names + one live REPL check with shutil.copyfile monkeypatched to raise OSError) demonstrates only the mid-copy-exception path, not the full 'under any input' claim the implementer result and handoff both assert. Independently probing an input class the evidence never covered (explainer_path=None or '') falsifies the broader claim -- see r1-handoff finding for the reproduction. The evidence presented is real but insufficient to support the claim it was offered for; it is not fabricated, just incomplete relative to the close criterion's actual scope ('under any input').

r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: General project-rule compliance is otherwise good: module-scope holds only immutable imports + a constant tuple (VALID_LANES), no module-level DatabaseManager singleton, library code has no print() calls, docstrings are thorough and cite exact source line numbers that check out. Primary fail carried up from r1-handoff/r3-evidence: explain_stage's 'never raises under any input' contract is violated for explainer_path=None/''. Secondary, non-blocking observation: optimize_stage's keyword defaults (lineup_size=10, beam_width=25, risk_percentile=90.0, balanced_risk_weight=0.25) are literal numbers that happen to match artifacts.py's DEFAULT_LINEUP_SIZE/DEFAULT_BEAM_WIDTH/DEFAULT_RISK_PERCENTILE/DEFAULT_BALANCED_RISK_WEIGHT (artifacts.py:27-30, exported in __all__) rather than importing/referencing those constants directly -- a silent-drift risk if artifacts.py's defaults ever change, not a functional bug today. Per-rule sub-checks appended as r4a/r4b/r4c to verify the handoff's named 'Constraints the Implementation Must Respect' individually.

r5-reconciliation.finding: No new src/ package, no new Cartographer-visible structural node -- struct:scripts is script-level and not map-visible per the handoff's own anchors. The implementer's Map Impact claims (consumes struct:evo_predictor/cmd_sampled_predict and struct:fantasy_scoring/generate_report unmodified; 3-lane restriction confirmed correct against source; design doc's 4-lane best_max mention confirmed stale) all check out against source. This is not architecture-significant enough to block the gate (a docs-only staleness, not a behavior/capability/constraint mismatch), but does need Commander's attention before the epic closes.

r4a-namespace-contract.title: SimpleNamespace matches cmd_sampled_predict argparse contract
r4a-namespace-contract.imperative: Verify predict_stage's SimpleNamespace fields (year, race, db_path, compound_prior_root/artifact, sampled_runtime_manifest, output) exactly match run.py:792-814's argparse dest names and cmd_sampled_predict's actual attribute usage. Record pass/fail.
r4a-namespace-contract.finding: Independently read run.py:792-814 (_add_sampled_predict_parser): dest names are sampled_runtime_manifest, year, race, compound_prior_root, compound_prior_artifact, db_path, output -- exact 1:1 match to predict_stage's SimpleNamespace(year=, race=, db_path=, compound_prior_root=, compound_prior_artifact=, sampled_runtime_manifest=, output=None). Also read cmd_sampled_predict body (run.py:544-563): uses args.year, args.race, getattr(args,'db_path',None), _compound_normalizer_for_sampled_predict(args) (getattr compound_prior_artifact/compound_prior_root), args.sampled_runtime_manifest, args.output -- every attribute it touches is present on the namespace predict_stage builds. No extra required attribute is missing.

r4b-xor-propagation.title: Compound-prior XOR ValueError propagates unswallowed
r4b-xor-propagation.imperative: Verify that when caller supplies neither compound_prior_root nor compound_prior_artifact, the ValueError from _compound_normalizer_for_sampled_predict is not caught/hidden by predict_stage. Record pass/fail.
r4b-xor-propagation.finding: Read _compound_normalizer_for_sampled_predict (run.py:522-541): raises ValueError('sampled runtime commands require --compound-prior-artifact or --compound-prior-root.') when neither is set, and a different ValueError when both are set. predict_stage has no try/except around cmd_sampled_predict(args) at all -- the call is bare (line 192: payload = cmd_sampled_predict(args)) so any exception propagates unmodified. Confirmed by test_predict_stage_propagates_compound_normalizer_valueerror, which I re-ran and which passed.
